title: Peer Pressure and Relationships
summary: Positive and negative peer pressure, assertiveness and refusal skills, qualities of healthy friendships, bullying and cyberbullying, and resolving conflict.

notes.text: The influence that people of your own age group have on your choices and behaviour.

Being dared to shoplift

headers: Example response to 'Come and smoke with us'
rows: Passive
Does not stand up for own rights or feelings; gives in
'Um… okay, I suppose.'
Aggressive
Stands up for self but disrespects or attacks others
'Are you stupid? Get lost!'
Assertive
Expresses own feelings and needs clearly and honestly while respecting others
'No thanks. I don't smoke. I'll see you at practice.'

items: Say **'No'** clearly and firmly; you do not have to give a long explanation.
Use confident **body language**: stand tall and make eye contact.
**Give a reason** if you want: 'I have a match tomorrow.'
**Suggest an alternative**: 'Let's go play soccer instead.'
Spend time with friends who share your values.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Use an **I-statement** to be assertive: 'I feel… when you… because… I would like…'. Example: 'I feel upset when you post photos of me without asking, because it is private. I would like you to take it down.'

rows: Respect, trust and honesty
Lies, jealousy and controlling behaviour
Both people can say no
Pressure, threats or manipulation
Open communication
Name-calling, humiliation or silent treatment
Support each other's goals and friendships
Isolating a person from friends and family

notes.text: **Bullying** is repeated, deliberate behaviour that hurts or frightens someone with less power. It can be **physical** (hitting), **verbal** (insults), **social** (excluding, spreading rumours) or online (**cyberbullying**: hurtful messages, posts, fake profiles or sharing private images).

items: If you are bullied: tell a trusted adult, keep evidence (screenshots), block and report the bully online, and do not retaliate.
If you see bullying: don't join in, support the victim and report it. Bystanders have power.
Help is available from Childline (**116**, free) and school counsellors.
Each person explains their side using I-statements, while the other **listens** without interrupting.
Agree on a fair solution (a **win–win** compromise) and follow it.

questions.prompt: What can a bystander do when they see someone being bullied?
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): don't join in or laugh; support the victim; tell a trusted adult/report it; encourage others to stand up

questions.prompt: Give TWO warning signs of an unhealthy relationship.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): jealousy/control; pressure or threats; name-calling; isolation from friends; dishonesty; violence
